components.css: .ds-thread { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; width: 280px; font: 600 14px Switzer, system-ui, sans-serif; color: #1a1a1a; } .ds-thread li { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 10px 0; } .ds-thread li:first-child { font-weight: 400; color: #444444; } .ds-thread b { width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 99px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px #ffffff; position: relative; z-index: 1; margin-left: 4px; } .ds-thread i { position: absolute; left: 9px; top: -14px; width: 3px; height: 30px; border-radius: 3px; } .ds-thread em { font-style: normal; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: .05em; text-transform: uppercase; }

narrative.overview: MeloMind is a bright, airy home screen where everything connects. Every pick hangs on a visible strand back to the thing you love that caused it, and the strand takes the colour of where it leads: amber for music, coral for film, blue for TV, green for books. The interface itself stays quiet and white so the covers and the threads do the talking.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, ink type, one amber accent for action and selection.
Four type colours used only as meaning: chips, thread strands, fallback tiles.
Chillax for anything that's a heading; Switzer for everything you read or tap.
Real Qloo images on every card; a designed gradient tile when there's none.
Motion is quiet: a 2 px lift on hover, a drawer that glides, a thread that grows once.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: A type colour appears only where it says what kind of thing this is. Never as decoration, never as a section background.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the single next action on a surface.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings speak for themselves: no kicker or label above a heading.

rules.name: The Chillax-Is-For-Headings Rule
rules.body: Chillax never sets a paragraph, a button label or a card title in a row.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Intent Rule
rules.body: A card has no shadow until the pointer is on it; then it rises 2 px and scales to 1.03. Never on touch devices.

dos: Do draw the thread wherever a pick has a source: rail, card strand, detail strip.
Do keep amber to the single next action on a surface.
Do use Qloo's image or the designed fallback tile on every card; rows never show an empty box.
Do label search links honestly ("Search on Netflix") and direct ones as "Open on".
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: fades replace movement.
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't use a type colour as decoration or a section background.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons; icons are Lucide, 1.75–2 px strokes.
Don't add a coloured stripe to the side of a card, list item or panel.
Don't show a disabled control without saying when it arrives ("Mood picks are coming soon").
